doc.name: A — skincare mask catalogue, travel context, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: clay mask jar
Category: skincare mask
Shot programme: travel context
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You run the tabletop stage for a premium skincare mask product shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the back-label view in a travel context treatment.

SUBJECT. A clay mask jar. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Rotated to show the reverse face, ingredient panel or hardware detail. Shoot on a 200mm compression telephoto at f/5.6, framing for deep negative space above the subject with a low horizon.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with split gel lighting, teal on the shadow side and magenta on the key side. Stage the product on or against mirrored steel, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a low-key grade holding detail in the deepest shadows only. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Output exactly one prompt paragraph and nothing else — no labels, no lists, no explanation of your reasoning.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
